analysis.title: GS Saboureault - Positioning Mondays Week 42 19 Oct 2026
key_insights: GS Global Equities PB book saw a -2.0 standard deviation (1-year) net selling event in the week to 16-Oct. All major regions were net sold, led in dollar terms by EM Asia and North America. Long sales outpaced short sales 2.6 to 1.

Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 4.2 pts to 48.6%, a 1-year low, and the desk puts it at the 1st percentile over 5 years. Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 1.4 pts to 210.9% (52nd percentile 1-year).

Info Tech was by far the most net sold global sector. It had the largest % de-grossing in 2 months and the largest % net selling on GS's record (since 2016), driven by long sales and to a lesser extent short sales. 8 of 11 global sectors were net sold, led in dollar terms by Info Tech, Industrials and Cons Disc. Health Care, Comm Svcs and Staples were the only net bought sectors.

Retail and traders took the other side. Global equity funds saw +$65bn net inflows (EPFR) vs +$12bn the prior week, driven by US funds and by technology funds. The SOX index had its worst week of the year (-11%), second worst behind Liberation Day, and nearly $10bn went into levered ETFs, with SOXL (3x semis) gathering a record +$7bn.
The SPX retail imbalance had its first negative day since July on Friday. The retail bid has been volatile.

Pre-US open Friday, GS models forecast decent CTA buying over 1 week and 1 month, mostly outside the US. The desk expects this probably changed after the SPX broke below its short-term threshold level during the session.

CTAs sold -$9.5bn of Global Equities over the past week, bringing length to about $39bn (42nd percentile). Models predict CTAs turn buyers on a 1-week horizon in a flat market, with buying rising on a 1-month horizon. FTSE100 and DAX see the largest inflows.
S&P E-mini levels to watch: 7716 (short-term threshold), 7508 (medium-term), 7040 (long-term).

Corporate bid is still subdued. The buyback desk reported 0.7x of 2025 YTD ADTV and 0.7x of 2024 YTD ADTV. 12% of the S&P 500 is in open window, moving to 22% by end of week. Flow was 85% 10b5-1 plans / 15% discretionary (vs 86%/14% prior week). The desk expects a pickup in November as the reporting calendar clears.

Europe flipped to risk-off after 3 consecutive weeks of risk-on, with long sells outpacing new shorts 1.8:1. Europe is overweight vs MSCI World by 2.84% (up 0.43 ppts WoW). North America is underweight at -15.77%, reduced by 1.62 ppts.

Sentiment is bearish on surveys. AAII bulls 38.7% (down 1.6 pts), bears 41.6% (up 2.6 pts), neutral 19.7%. The CNN Fear & Greed Index fell to 18/100 (Extreme Fear) from 46/100 the prior week. The GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator rose to -0.4 from -0.7.
META, TSLA and NVDA (GTC Berlin) are the key micro events this week, all on Wednesday.

sector_views.rationale: Most net sold global sector in the GS PB book, with the largest % net selling on record since 2016 and the largest % de-grossing in 2 months. This is a flow observation, not a formal rating.

sector_views.sector: Health Care, Communication Services, Consumer Staples
sector_views.rationale: The only three of 11 global sectors that were net bought in the GS PB book last week.

earnings_insights: Buyback blackout is in effect. The reporting calendar is heavily weighted to late October, and the desk expects the lighter buyback pace to continue near term and to pick up in November.
risk_factors: Retail dip-buying into the tech sell-off, including record levered semis ETF inflows, leaves a crowded retail long exposed if semis keep falling.
A break below the S&P E-mini short-term threshold (7716) could change the expected CTA flows from buying to selling.
Buyback support stays thin until open windows widen in November.
Heavy institutional de-grossing in Info Tech could continue.
vol_and_positioning: Overall book gross leverage rose 3.0 pts to 311.7% (79th percentile 1-year). Net leverage fell 3.2 pts to 72.7% (4th percentile 1-year). L/S ratio fell 2.6% to 1.609 (4th percentile 1-year).
Fundamental L/S net leverage at 48.6% is a 1-year low and sits at the 1st percentile over 5 years.
Asset managers were small net buyers of S&P futures in the week ending October 13 (CFTC).
The SOX fell 11% in its worst week of the year. Levered ETF inflows were nearly $10bn, with a record +$7bn into SOXL.
CTA length in Global Equities is about $39bn (42nd percentile) after $9.5bn of selling over the week.
SPX broke below its short-term CTA threshold level (7716) during Friday's session. Medium-term level is 7508 and long-term is 7040.

tension_points.bull_case: Retail and mutual funds are buying the tech sell-off. Global equity funds took in +$65bn, led by US and technology funds, and SOXL drew a record +$7bn. CTAs are modeled to turn buyers over 1 week and 1 month in a flat market. Buybacks are expected to pick up in November.
tension_points.bear_case: Hedge funds sold technology at record pace (the largest % net selling since 2016) and Fundamental L/S net leverage is at the 1st percentile over 5 years. The SPX broke below its short-term CTA threshold, the corporate bid is subdued, and the retail bid is volatile with the first negative SPX retail imbalance day since July.
tension_points.what_invalidates: SPX holding below the 7716 short-term threshold, which the desk says probably changed the expected CTA buying, with 7508 (medium-term) and 7040 (long-term) as the next levels.
